mainEntity.name: Can functional medicine help with stubborn weight?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We treat weight by addressing what is holding it on, insulin, thyroid, hormones, and stress, rather than blaming willpower. Most people find the scale responds again as the root causes are corrected.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer GLP-1 medications like semaglutide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Where it is appropriate, yes. We use GLP-1 support as one tool inside a full plan, paired with nutrition and root-cause work so the results last beyond the medication.

mainEntity.name: What testing do you run for weight and metabolism?

acceptedAnswer.text: We go beyond a basic panel, with in six months, A1c, full thyroid, hormones, and inflammation markers, so the plan targets your specific root causes.

mainEntity.name: Why can I not lose weight even when I eat well?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often the issue is insulin resistance, thyroid, or hormones quietly telling your body to store rather than burn. When we correct those, eating well finally starts to work.
Severe restriction slows metabolism. We build a sustainable plan around your labs so your body feels safe enough to let the weight go.
Our goal is lasting change, so we treat the cause and adjust as your metabolism improves. That is what helps progress hold rather than rebound.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer virtual weight care or only in person in Atlanta?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both. See Dr. Nina Ross in person at our Atlanta clinic, or virtually anywhere in Georgia. Your $99 Symptom Consultation can be booked either way.

sections.label: Hero

headings.text: Root-cause weight and metabolism care in Atlanta that finally makes your body respond.

paragraphs: If you are eating well, moving more and the scale still will not move, or it climbs while you do everything right, you are not imagining it.

The struggle is real, and it deserves someone who will listen to the whole story. At Nina Ross Functional Medicine, we treat weight at its root, here in Atlanta and virtually across Georgia. Dr. Nina Ross follows the whole picture, insulin, thyroid, and the hormones behind a stalled metabolism, until she finds what is really holding your weight on, then builds the plan around your body and your life.

sections.label: Why conventional care misses it

headings.text: You were told to eat less and move more.

eyebrowSpans: Why conventional care keeps missing it
paragraphs: A fifteen-minute visit rarely has room to look at the whole metabolism. So weight gets blamed on willpower, and the thing holding it on goes unexamined.

boldPairs.title: What you’re usually told
boldPairs.body: “Just eat less and move more. It really is that simple.”

boldPairs.title: What’s actually happening
boldPairs.body: Insulin, thyroid, and stress hormones are working against you in a loop. Correct the loop and your metabolism responds again.

sections.label: The functional medicine difference

headings.text: We will not blame your willpower and call it a plan.

paragraphs: Here is where we part ways with conventional care. When the weight will not move, the reflex answer is a stricter diet and more discipline, or a medication handed over with no map of why your metabolism stalled. A crash diet can drop a few pounds. But under-eating a stalled metabolism teaches your body to conserve, and the weight returns the moment real life resumes.
We would rather do the harder, more honest work. We find what is actually holding your weight on and we treat that.
If a medication like a GLP-1 still has a place in your plan, that should be your informed choice, made with the full picture in front of you, and paired with the work that makes it last.

boldPairs.title: It blames effort, not biology
boldPairs.body: Being told to try harder ignores the insulin and hormones quietly holding your weight on.

boldPairs.title: Crash diets can slow you further
boldPairs.body: Severe restriction signals scarcity, and your body answers by burning less.

boldPairs.title: A pill alone postpones the fix
boldPairs.body: Medication without a root-cause plan tends to fade the moment you stop taking it.

sections.label: The root-cause view

headings.text: Stubborn weight runs in a loop. We map the whole circle.

paragraphs: Each driver pushes the next. That is why treating one in isolation rarely holds, and why mapping the full cycle changes everything.
When we investigate your metabolism, we read the whole hormonal and metabolic picture rather than a single number, and connect each driver back to what you’re feeling:

strongBullets.label: Insulin resistance
strongBullets.full: Insulin resistance, the engine that stores fat and blocks the body from burning it.

strongBullets.label: An underactive thyroid
strongBullets.full: An underactive thyroid, the slow metabolism, the cold hands, and the stalled scale.

strongBullets.label: Cortisol & stress
strongBullets.full: Cortisol & stress, that parks weight around the middle and drives cravings.

strongBullets.label: Hormone shifts
strongBullets.full: Hormone shifts, where perimenopause and low hormones change how you store weight.

strongBullets.label: Blood sugar swings
strongBullets.full: Blood sugar swings, behind the hunger, the crashes, and the late-day snacking.

strongBullets.label: Poor sleep
strongBullets.full: Poor sleep, that raises hunger hormones and lowers the will to move.

strongBullets.label: Chronic inflammation
strongBullets.full: Chronic inflammation, the quiet driver that keeps metabolism stuck.
